evals.prompt: /doxxnet help
evals.expected_output: Prints the capability menu and asks what the user wants to do
expectations: Displays all capability areas with short descriptions, including Cloud Servers
Mentions /network-wizard for guided setup
Does not make any API calls
Asks the user what they want to do

evals.prompt: Show me my tunnels and current bandwidth usage
evals.expected_output: Tunnel list plus bandwidth stats
expectations: Calls list_tunnels and shows only names, servers, addresses and connection state (no tunnel_token or private_key)
Calls /api/stats/bandwidth for recent bandwidth (default last hour)
Passes Stats API params in the query string with the token in the X-Auth-Token header (stdin), never in the URL
Presents tunnel status and bandwidth together, keyed by tunnel name

evals.prompt: Enable ad blocking on all my devices and show me what's currently being blocked
evals.expected_output: DNS blocking enabled plus alert summary
expectations: Calls dns_get_options to list available blocklists
Calls dns_set_subscription with apply_to_all to enable blocking
Calls /api/stats/alerts?last=1d to show current blocks
Shows category_counts and block_count

evals.prompt: Open port 443 on my server and check if the tunnel is connected
evals.expected_output: Firewall rule added and tunnel status shown
expectations: Calls list_tunnels to find the server tunnel and its IP
Calls firewall_rule_add with protocol=TCP and dst_port=443
Shows tunnel connection status from list_tunnels response

evals.prompt: Give me a full overview of my network
evals.expected_output: Comprehensive network dashboard
expectations: Calls list_tunnels for device status (fields only)
Calls /api/stats/bandwidth, /api/stats/alerts and /api/stats/summary
Passes Stats API params in the query string with the token in the X-Auth-Token header (stdin), never in the URL
Maps stats tunnel tokens to tunnel names and never prints them
Presents a unified dashboard-style summary

evals.prompt: Show me all my devices and which ones are online
evals.expected_output: Lists all devices with online/offline status
expectations: Calls device_list_unified with the user's auth token
Shows each device with name, model, OS, and online status
Highlights which devices are currently online
Shows seats used of total

evals.prompt: Show me my IP addresses and rotate my public one
evals.expected_output: Explains a dedicated IPv4 cannot be rotated; offers alternatives
expectations: Calls list_addresses to show all assigned IPs
Explains that a dedicated public IPv4 cannot be rotated (rotate_address takes static_private or static_ipv6 only)
Offers the options that exist instead (rotate a private or IPv6 address, or release and lease a new dedicated IPv4), with confirmation

evals.prompt: What subscription am I on and generate recovery codes
evals.expected_output: Reads the plan from live entitlements and sends the user to the portal for recovery codes
expectations: Reads the plan and seats from POST https://payments.doxx.net/v1/access/status, not from a Config API endpoint
Calls only endpoints in the public manifest and sends the user to the portal for recovery codes
Sends the user to the portal profile page (https://app.doxx.net/ops/account/profile) to create recovery codes
Explains the codes are the backup for a lost token and that redeeming one revokes every token

evals.prompt: build me a VPN
evals.expected_output: Asks whether the user wants quick or full setup, then runs the wizard inline
expectations: Recognizes setup intent from natural language without an explicit command
Offers quick vs full mode choice with descriptions
Checks for an existing auth token before proceeding
Follows the appropriate wizard phases based on the user's mode choice

evals.prompt: Set up a new tunnel in New York and install WireGuard on my Mac
evals.expected_output: Creates a tunnel on a New York server, writes the WireGuard config to /etc/wireguard/doxx.conf, and activates it
expectations: Calls servers and picks a New York server
Calls create_tunnel with that server and type=wireguard
Fetches the config with wireguard into a private temp directory without printing the private key
Installs it with sudo install -m 600 to /etc/wireguard/doxx.conf and runs sudo wg-quick up doxx
Cleans up the temp directory afterwards

evals.prompt: Lease a dedicated IPv4 address for my iPhone tunnel
evals.expected_output: Leases a dedicated public IPv4 and applies it to the iPhone tunnel without asking the user about profiles
expectations: Checks the entitlements for a free dedicated IP slot first
Calls list_tunnels to identify the iPhone tunnel and its active_profile_id
Calls lease_public_ipv4 with profile_id, or with profile_name and server when the tunnel has no profile
Confirms before load_profile, because it replaces the tunnel's settings
Presents the leased ip_address and any requires_reconnect notice without exposing profile mechanics

evals.prompt: Show me my bandwidth usage for the last 7 days and any security alerts
evals.expected_output: Returns bandwidth stats for the 7-day window plus a security alert summary
expectations: Calls /api/stats/bandwidth with start 7 days ago (RFC3339 UTC) in the query string, or /api/stats/summary?days=7
Calls /api/stats/alerts?last=7d
Presents peak bandwidth in Mbps per tunnel name
Groups alerts by category (ads, tracking, malware, security)

evals.prompt: Register a .vpn domain and create an A record pointing to my tunnel IP
evals.expected_output: Registers a .vpn domain and creates a DNS A record pointing to the tunnel's assigned IP
expectations: Checks list_tlds that .vpn exists
Calls create_domain to register the domain
Calls list_tunnels to get the tunnel's assigned IP
Calls create_dns_record with type=A and the tunnel IP as content
Handles domain_limit by sending the user to the portal instead of retrying

evals.prompt: Link all my tunnels together for mesh networking
evals.expected_output: Enables full mesh networking across all tunnels
expectations: Calls list_tunnels to confirm tunnels exist
Calls firewall_link_all_toggle with enabled=1
Confirms mesh is active via firewall_link_all_status
Reports which tunnels are now linked

evals.prompt: Rotate my private IP address and update any DNS records that reference it
evals.expected_output: Rotates the static IP and updates all DNS A records that pointed to the old IP
expectations: Calls list_addresses to identify the static_private address
Warns the user that the old IP is released for good, and gets confirmation
Calls rotate_address and reads new_address
Calls list_domains and list_dns for each domain to find A records pointing to the old IP
Calls update_dns_record for each affected record with the new IP

evals.prompt: Set up my tunnel in the WireGuard app on my phone
evals.expected_output: Generates a WireGuard QR code for the user to scan in the WireGuard app
expectations: Calls list_tunnels to identify the relevant tunnel
Verifies the tunnel is a generic WireGuard tunnel (not a native doxx.net app tunnel)
Builds doxx.conf from the wireguard response in a private temp directory without printing the key
Offers a local QR code (qrencode) or the .conf file: makes the QR code locally and never sends the config to a server to render it
Instructs the user to scan it in the WireGuard app

evals.prompt: Rename my agent Fable to Atlas and move it to my Linux server
evals.expected_output: Routes to update_agent with confirmation
expectations: Calls list_agents and device_list_unified to resolve agent_id and the server's device_hash
Warns that re-hosting revokes the current host's credentials at once and that the new name is shown to every pair
Calls update_agent with agent_id, agent_name and host_device_hash after confirmation

evals.prompt: What's my current public IP and ISP?
evals.expected_output: One network_info call
expectations: Calls network_info once and shows ip, asn and org
Does not use a third-party IP lookup service

evals.prompt: Set up a cloud server for me
evals.expected_output: Routes to manage-vps
expectations: Routes cloud server work to the manage-vps skill
Does not quote server prices from memory (reads vps_catalog live)
Checks the entitlements: a cloud server needs the VPS add-on, which any plan can buy (Free included); does not say Pro is required

evals.prompt: Create a token for my automation script
evals.expected_output: Explicit role, private file
expectations: Calls create_token with an explicit role (net-admin) and expires_at, knowing the default is read-only
Saves new_token to a 0600 file and never prints it
